cwe: CWE-59 Link Following / CWE-22 Path Traversal
title: Arbitrary file write outside the extraction directory via symlink entries in extract-zip
shortFix: Patches CVE-2026-56876 and CVE-2026-19693 (symlink path traversal / arbitrary file write): symlinks may only point inside the target directory, and files are never written through a symlink.
longFix: Symlink entries are resolved the way the operating system will resolve them — from the real directory containing the link, following symlinks that already exist — and rejected unless they land inside the extraction directory. Absolute link targets, and targets with a `..` after a normal segment (which can escape through a symlinked segment), are rejected outright. Before writing a file or creating a link, any symlink already sitting at that path is removed rather than followed.
summary: extract-zip validated only the parent directory of each archive entry. A malicious zip could (1) create a symlink pointing anywhere on disk (CVE-2026-56876), and (2) follow it with a regular file of the same name, which extract-zip then wrote through the symlink — an arbitrary file write outside the extraction directory (CVE-2026-19693). Any service that extracts user-supplied zips (uploads, plugin/theme installers, CI artefacts, Electron updaters) is exposed.
fixExplanation: Three checks, each covered by a regression test that fails on 2.0.1: (1) every symlink target is resolved against the real filesystem and must land inside the target directory; absolute targets and `x/../y`-style targets are refused, closing bypasses of a purely textual check (e.g. a link through an earlier `d -> .` symlink); (2) an existing symlink at a destination path is removed before writing, never written through; (3) the existing parent-directory check is kept and also guards against cross-drive paths on Windows. Normal archives — files, nested folders, file modes, `__MACOSX` skipping, and relative symlinks that stay inside (as in macOS .app/framework bundles) — extract exactly as before.
